evidence: PlaceOrderUseCase.ts: private mapToDto(order) returns { id, status: order.getStatus(), lines: order.lines, createdAt: order.createdAt.toISOString() }.
CancelOrderUseCase.ts: execute ends with an inline copy of the same object literal.
ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.ts: orders.map(order => ({ id, status, lines, createdAt })) repeats the mapping.
UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.ts: the same inline mapping appears a fourth time.

UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.ts: const validStatuses: OrderStatus[] = ['placed','paid','packed','shipped','delivered'] and the cast request.status as OrderStatus re-declare the status set outside the domain.
GetStockLevelsUseCase.ts maps products to ProductStockDto inline, so the module has no shared mapper convention.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The five use cases serve one concern, order and stock operations in the application layer. They share one shape: a class with constructor-injected ports and an `execute` method. But the Order-to-OrderDto mapping is copied into four files instead of living in one place. `UpdateOrderStatusUseCase` also hard-codes a list of valid statuses, which is a domain rule. That list duplicates the `OrderStatus` knowledge held by the `Order` entity, which already validates in `transitionTo`.

violations.message: Defines a private mapToDto that duplicates the Order to OrderDto mapping also found inline in the Cancel, List and Update use cases. The mapping should live in one shared mapper.
